text:
maya: Heads up — release/1.14.0 is blocked, CI failed during publish. Looks like shared-deps cache TTL expired and we pulled a mismatched wheel for grpcio.
sam: Can you paste the failing job link?
ci-runner: Job 3821 failed: error: incompatible wheel for grpcio==1.51.0 on linux_x86_64, sha mismatch. Logs snippet:
```
ERROR: Hash mismatch for /cache/wheels/grpcio-1.51.0.whl
Expected: sha256:abcd1234...
Got: sha256:efgh5678...
```
maya: That's odd — TTL is set to 7d. Could the mirror have rotated different wheel variants?
aditya: We've seen upstream mirror inconsistencies before (manylinux2014 vs manylinux2014_py38). My hunch: mirror returned a wheel built with different tags which changed the hash. Suggest pinning wheel hash in constraints for the release branch.
rosie: How urgent is this? Can we just rerun CI after purging the cache? @deploy-bot any objections to holding the window?
deploy-bot: Rollback available: `rollback release/1.14.0 -> release/1.13.5`. Manual approval required. Command: `/deploy rollback release/1.14.0 --approve` + codeowner signoff.
sam: I'd rather rerun CI after purging the cached wheel to force a rebuild. Proposed command: `ci-cache purge shared-deps --key grpcio-1.51.0`. @ci-runner can you trigger a purge and rerun?
ci-runner: Purge queued. Re-run triggered: https://ci.example.com/builds/3822. ETA ~6m.
maya: If the rerun passes, follow-ups: 1) pin hashed wheel in constraints for release branch, 2) bump cache TTL to 14d, 3) add a short note in release notes about transient mirror mismatch.
aditya: I'll open a PR to add the pinned hash and increase TTL; target: hotfix post-merge to avoid blocking current release. If rerun fails, we'll do the rollback path.
rosie: :thumbsup: I'll hold the change window until 12:30 UTC and notify stakeholders.
ci-runner: Build 3822 succeeded — tests green, artifact pushed to staging.
maya: Great. Proceeding with release now. Opening follow-up PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/pkgs/constraints/pulls/487 (adds pin + TTL bump).
sam: Nice work. We'll keep monitoring for 24h. Thanks everyone.
